FT-002.adaptation: Accepted FT-002 rev 7: standing compiler bottleneck repair at 5KB/50KB/500KB with p50/p95/p99, superlinear hot-path removal, and proof that incremental equals clean. Directly relevant precedent on this branch: rev 6 re-measurement already caught a quadratic reuse lookup that had pushed a one-word edit to 178 ms p95, so the superlinear risk is real and measured, not hypothetical. Open issue #21 reports a valid 500KB project exceeding the runtime output frame limit, which is the same scale boundary this revision targets; will read and address it as part of this work.

next_action: Available for dispatch. Remaining known bottleneck is that every keystroke still reparses the whole document; incremental parsing would be the next structural step.

origin/main.adaptation: I chased the wrong suspect twice before measuring properly. I first indexed the reuse candidate lookup and then made candidate shifting lazy, which together bought only 474->420 ms. Measuring the parse share showed parse was 402 of the 420 ms, so the reuse machinery was never the problem. The actual cause was that every macro invocation removed its token and then spliced the expansion into the gap, moving the token tail twice per invocation.

summary: FT-002 rev 7 delivered: scaling benchmark at 5KB/50KB/500KB with p50/p95/p99 and input+binary hashes, and a 14x speedup from removing a quadratic in the parser. A 500KB one-word edit went from 420.606 ms to 29.401 ms p95 and scaling is now approximately linear. Incremental equals clean full build at all three sizes.
